commit a07c7fd522ef0a897601c114f927a49d93d95520 (2026-10-17, "Add MIT license")
vendored v4880 (a SPIKE, unnumbered until shipped): ocean.html ONLY, byte-identical to upstream's published single-file bundle -- 102,283 bytes,
sha256 61e4fe5edf10253b0552570b574da7206754c2fb6033e2e6d73845daae4b36e8. Not modified in any way. Upstream's js/ sources, the minified bundle (ocean.min.html), the
build files and the README images were NOT taken: the bundle is self-contained and is what the spike embeds.
WHAT IT IS: a real-time WebGPU ocean written without an engine -- a six-cascade 256x256 FFT sea (JONSWAP wind sea plus a swell), a CDLOD surface mesh, whitecaps and
foam, a Hillaire-style atmosphere with two cloud layers, HDR with bloom and AgX tone mapping. Its README says it was built with Claude Code.
WHAT THE BUNDLE DOES NOT DO: it makes no network request (the file contains no http string), owns its canvas, camera, sky and post-processing, and reads the
water height under its camera back from the GPU a few frames late. See ocean-spike.html for what that means for using it.
VERIFIED BY READING AND BY HASH, NOT BY RUNNING: the sandbox this was vendored in has no WebGPU adapter, so the page was not seen to render here. The hash is the
only claim; tools/ship/oceanSpikePage-selfcheck.mjs holds the file to it.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDED v4895 (unnumbered until shipped): THE MODULAR SOURCES the bundle above is built from, taken byte for byte from the same repository (raw.githubusercontent.com, main):
  index.html, build.mjs, js/main.js, js/wgsl/common.js, js/wgsl/sim.js, js/wgsl/sky.js, js/wgsl/ocean.js, js/wgsl/post.js        (LICENSE was already here and is identical to upstream's)
PROVED, NOT ASSUMED: running upstream's own readable-bundle rule over these files (build.mjs: strip each file's import lines and the `export` keyword, concatenate in the order
common, sim, sky, ocean, post, main, drop the result into index.html in place of its <script src="js/main.js"> tag) reproduces ocean.html BYTE FOR BYTE (102,283 bytes, sha256
61e4fe5e...). tools/ship/oceanSrcRebuild-selfcheck.mjs redoes that rebuild on every run and pins every file's sha256, so a changed source, a changed rule or a changed bundle goes red.
WHAT THE SOURCES ADD: `export const P` in js/main.js. The bundle's build strips that `export`, which is why P is invisible INSIDE the bundle -- but upstream applies every P key from the
URL anyway (the loop on the bundle's line 2193), so the sea is tunable from the query string either way. v4890 and v4894 said the opposite and were wrong; see ui/oceanSea.mjs.
CORRECTION TO THE PARAGRAPH ABOVE: "it makes no network request" is not true. js/main.js makes three calls, all POSTs to the page's OWN origin: log() sends each log line to /__log, and the
?shot= screenshot path sends the image to /__shot twice over. The engine's server answers /__log with a 404; /__shot is reached only when a page is loaded with ?shot=. The file
contains no http string and nothing leaves the origin; they are still requests, and tools/ship/oceanSrcRebuild-selfcheck.mjs counts them.
NOT TAKEN: upstream's server.mjs, ocean.min.html, package.json/package-lock.json, docs/ and README (nothing here runs a build, and esbuild is not a dependency of this tree).
NOTHING IN THE ENGINE IMPORTS THESE FILES YET. They are here so a later round can adapt them (expose the water height the shader already computes, set the parameters
programmatically, composite SweK objects against the sea) with the upstream bytes beside the changes and a gate that says exactly what moved.

----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
ADDED v4895, STEP 2 (unnumbered until shipped): THE SENTENCE "NOTHING IN THE ENGINE IMPORTS THESE FILES YET" ABOVE IS NO LONGER TRUE. tools/ship/seaPatch.mjs is a recorded list of three patches over js/main.js
(the five './wgsl/' imports made absolute; `export const seaApi`, a setParams that sets any key of upstream's P -- swellSpread, which has no panel slider, included -- and raises the flag upstream raises;
a three-line hook that gives the api its closure over the flags and over waterH) and world/ocean/seaMain.mjs is the generated result. NO BYTE IN THIS DIRECTORY CHANGED: the vendored files are still
the pinned upstream bytes, and tools/ship/seaPatch-selfcheck.mjs runs the patches backwards on seaMain.mjs to prove it. No page loads seaMain.mjs yet; ocean-sea.html still loads the single-file bundle.
